tasks.short: Organize and write technical material to agreed structure, style, clarity, and terminology standards.

steps.what: Gather approved specifications, existing instructions, and reference material from the {DOCS}.
Choose the reader tasks, scope, sequence, and document outline.
Draft explanations and procedures using the content plan and source pack.

loop.input: Approved source pack, content plan, document template, and terminology base.
loop.output: Technical draft with source references and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, values, units, and source references; writer reviews meaning and procedure sequence.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unresolved facts return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but varied source prose needs synthesis into reader instructions.

steps.what: Check technical accuracy, operating sequence, and safety instructions.
Apply terminology, heading, numbering, and formatting standards.
Resolve remaining issues and accept the manuscript for publication preparation.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles versioned sources from the {DOCS}, while templates and a bounded drafting loop produce source-linked sections. Configured checks produce a quality report in the {DOCS}; technical approval and manuscript acceptance remain separate human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source versions were scattered, templates covered only structure, and technical synthesis still required substantial writing.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building source connectors and document generators. Bounded drafting can work within an approved source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Sources may omit operating conditions. Correct-looking instructions still need technical validation, especially where mistakes could harm people.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what readers must accomplish and recognize when an apparently clear instruction is unsafe or incomplete.
tasks.altitude: The writer spends more time testing explanations with users and resolving source gaps. Technical approval and publication decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare accessible manual layouts from structured content.
reach.learn: Semantic headings, reusable page structures, and accessible tables.

evidence.claim: Acrolinx supports repeatable style checks and quality gates.
A trial found gains in professional writing; it did not establish technical-manual accuracy or safety.
Source assembly, templates, and bounded drafting can be combined; effort and remaining-time estimates are planning assumptions.

assumptions: A typical company uses the {DOCS} for drafting and technical review.
Time shares are illustrative, with document work dominant as the priors suggest.
Collection requires approved source locations and version identifiers.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; national rules determine any employee consultation.
unknowns: Which sources are authoritative and accessible?
Who approves safety instructions and final manuscripts?
Does the {DOCS} support templates, tracked changes, and configured quality checks?
Which confidentiality restrictions and consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which manual sections can be generated from structured specifications alone?
How often do drafts introduce unsupported conditions or omit prerequisites?
Can operators complete representative tasks using the generated instructions?
new_work: Review source references and unresolved information gaps.
Maintain templates, terminology, and source connectors.
Revalidate instructions when sources or drafting rules change.
tasks.statement: Organize material and complete writing assignment according to set standards regarding order, clarity, conciseness, style, and terminology.

tasks.short: Keep writing files, revision histories, and approved versions traceable and retrievable.

steps.what: Save the latest working file in the shared {DOCS}.
Update document identifiers, version labels, status, and source links.
Record revision dates, contributors, and change references in the revision log.
Confirm the approved version and mark previous versions as superseded.

tasks.design: Configure version history, required metadata, and approval states in the {DOCS}. Use that history as the revision log, and make superseding a version a controlled transition that preserves earlier records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local copies and inconsistent naming weakened version history. Separate logs repeated information already stored with files.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls can often handle this through configuration. Small deterministic adapters can connect approval records where needed.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting legacy copies, unclear ownership, and inconsistent retention rules require cleanup and decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed provenance and decide which version represents the approved technical position.

ambition.what: Self-service document lineage lookup for customer support staff

tasks.altitude: Routine saving and logging largely disappear, leaving short exception reviews and occasional record cleanup. Decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check that a manuscript uses the correct approved source version.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, approval states, and revision lineage.

evidence.claim: Version history, required metadata, and approval states are established document-management capabilities.
A separate revision log can be removed when native history captures the required fields; estimates require local validation.

assumptions: The {DOCS} holds most working files, although some copies still require reconciliation.
Required change references can link to review records without model-generated summaries.
Superseding a version preserves it; deletion is outside this design.
GDPR applies to contributor records. National rules may require consultation if logging changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Does native history meet contractual and retention requirements?
How many uncontrolled copies and conflicting identifiers exist?
Which metadata can be inherited reliably?
Who may change approval states and record access?
research_questions: Can native history replace all required revision-log fields?
Can representative users retrieve the approved version and its review evidence?
What exceptions remain after a small legacy-document migration?
new_work: Resolve missing identifiers and conflicting versions.
Maintain metadata rules, permissions, and approval transitions.
Check broken source links and periodically test retrieval.
tasks.statement: Maintain records and files of work and revisions.

tasks.short: Edit colleagues' technical material for consistency, clarity, and accurate meaning.

steps.what: Collect the contributor draft, references, and editing brief through the {EMAIL}.
Check spelling, terminology, references, and house-style compliance.
Restructure unclear passages and propose edits while preserving technical meaning.

loop.input: Contributor draft, source pack, style rules, and quality report.
loop.output: Tracked edits with reasons and queries for ambiguous technical statements.
loop.check: Compare numbers, units, identifiers, warnings, and conditions; writer reviews semantic changes.
loop.stop: One edit pass and one repair pass per section; unresolved meaning becomes an author query.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules identify standard violations but cannot reliably restructure varied prose while preserving its intended meaning.

steps.what: Discuss ambiguous statements and confirm corrections to technical meaning.
Accept agreed edits and hand over the approved manuscript.

tasks.design: A submission flow in the {WORKFLOW} places drafts and references in the {DOCS}, where configured checks run first. A bounded editing loop proposes tracked changes and author queries; technical corrections and final acceptance receive their respective human approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule checkers handled surface consistency, while mixed-quality drafts and ambiguous meaning still required extensive manual editing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured checks can be combined with bounded rewriting and deterministic comparisons of protected technical values.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent rewrite can change a qualification, warning, or operating condition. Conflicting expert opinions still need resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether clearer wording preserves the author's intended technical claim and the reader's ability to act safely.
tasks.altitude: The writer reviews proposed changes and spends more time resolving meaning with contributors. Editorial and technical approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare translation updates from approved technical changes.
reach.learn: Term-base structure, translation context, and stable segment identifiers.

evidence.claim: LanguageTool checks spelling, grammar, punctuation, and style.
Acrolinx provides house-style scoring and quality gates.
A vendor case reports fewer translation edits; it does not establish savings for this workflow.
Protected-value comparisons and tracked model edits can support human editing; remaining-time estimates are unvalidated.

assumptions: Drafts commonly arrive through the {EMAIL}, while most editing happens in the {DOCS}.
Style rules and approved terminology can be separated from technical meaning decisions.
The high automation prior is moderated because semantic changes still require review.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; any employee consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Which edits may be accepted without technical reapproval?
Are tracked changes preserved across the actual document formats?
Which values, warnings, and terms require exact preservation?
Can the source material be processed within approved confidentiality controls?
research_questions: Which edit categories are safe for deterministic correction?
How often do proposed rewrites alter technical meaning?
Do change packs reduce clarification requests from translators?
new_work: Review semantic changes and resolve author queries.
Maintain style rules, protected terms, and edit examples.
Investigate recurring false positives and missed technical changes.
tasks.statement: Edit, standardize, or make changes to material prepared by other writers or establishment personnel.

tasks.short: Agree technical specifications and publication scope with customers, suppliers and internal technical owners.

steps.what: Collect existing specifications, customer requests and previous publication decisions.
Prepare questions about users, technical limits, publication scope and unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Selected source documents and a fixed requirements checklist.
loop.output: Cited background summary and questions about missing or conflicting requirements.
loop.check: Validate source references; separate known requirements from assumptions; writer selects the questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing sources produce explicit questions; writer handles unresolved conflicts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A checklist supplies headings but cannot identify contradictions in varied customer and technical prose.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and share the agenda with participants.
Discuss intended use, technical constraints and publication scope with stakeholders.
Write the scope brief, decisions, open questions and assigned actions.

loop.input: Writer's discussion notes, provisional scope and approved source documents.
loop.output: Scope brief distinguishing agreed decisions, proposals and open questions.
loop.check: Link requirements to notes or sources; reject inferred agreement; writer confirms owners and commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; ambiguous agreement remains open; writer completes unresolved wording.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation to distinguish commitments from suggestions; templates alone cannot do that.

steps.what: Confirm technical commitments and send the scope brief for stakeholder acceptance.

tasks.design: A controlled job assembles relevant records from the {DOCS}, {CRM} and {EMAIL}, then a bounded loop drafts a cited agenda. People conduct the discussion; another bounded loop turns their notes into a scope brief in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes technical approval, sends the approved acceptance request and records stakeholder responses before scope is treated as accepted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived through conversations and inconsistent documents. Scheduling and paperwork were separate from the human work of clarifying needs and negotiating scope.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar workflows and structured scope forms handle coordination. Bounded drafting can organise supplied notes without assuming that ambiguous statements are agreements.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may disagree or leave essential constraints unstated. Technical commitments, customer acceptance and sensitive supplier information require deliberate human handling.
tasks.human_edge: The writer asks follow-up questions, recognises hesitation and negotiates a scope people can actually deliver.

ambition.what: Operator comprehension briefing before publication scope is finalised.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more of the week clarifying reader needs and less assembling agendas and minutes. They can lead requirements discovery; technical commitments and customer acceptance keep their existing decision owners.

reach.task: Interview operators about confusing instructions.
reach.learn: Neutral questioning, sampling and separating observations from assumptions.

reach.task: Define publication audiences and intended outcomes.
reach.learn: Audience segmentation and prioritising competing stakeholder needs.

evidence.claim: A writing trial found faster professional drafting; it did not test technical-scope negotiation.
Source-linked agenda and scope drafting are plausible bounded uses of models, subject to local validation.
Scheduling, approval routing and acceptance tracking can use configured workflows.

assumptions: The conversation-heavy priors are retained; preparation and paperwork are separate opportunities.
The pilot uses written notes and does not require recording participants.
Records can be retrieved using known project and customer identifiers.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; customer, employee and supplier data require controlled processing.
Access effort includes employee consultation where national rules apply; elapsed approval time can be longer.
unknowns: Who can commit to technical specifications and accept publication scope.
Whether external stakeholders require a particular acceptance process.
Confidentiality restrictions on customer and supplier documents.
Available access to relevant records and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Does scope drafting preserve the distinction between proposals and agreed commitments?
Which agenda questions reveal missing requirements before the main discussion?
new_work: Verify meeting notes, commitments and action owners.
Resolve conflicting requirements and track outstanding acceptance.
Maintain scope templates, retrieval filters and access permissions.
Review model errors and prevent inferred agreement from entering approved records.
tasks.statement: Confer with customer representatives, vendors, plant executives, or publisher to establish technical specifications and to determine subject material to be developed for publication.

tasks.short: Review published technical material and recommend changes to content, scope, format and production.

steps.what: Collect published editions, current specifications, reader feedback and production requirements.
Annotate outdated instructions, terminology problems, omissions and inconsistencies.

loop.input: Published passages, corresponding approved specifications, style guide and term list.
loop.output: Rule violations and possible substantive discrepancies, each linked to source passages.
loop.check: Validate version identifiers and citations; distinguish exact mismatches from uncertain interpretations; writer reviews findings.
loop.stop: One comparison pass and one correction pass per section; unresolved or unsupported findings enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch terminology and version differences; changed technical meaning requires interpreting prose.

steps.what: Decide which issues justify changes in scope, content or format.
Write revision recommendations with examples and reasons.

loop.input: Writer-selected priorities, approved source passages and revision brief template.
loop.output: Proposed changes with supporting sources, examples and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require sources for technical claims; check terminology; writer confirms recommendations preserve technical meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims remain questions; writer completes unresolved recommendations.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief but cannot explain varied prose changes or their consequences.

steps.what: Discuss revision scope and production options with technical and publication owners.
Approve the revision brief and assign follow-up work.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles version-linked material from the {DOCS}, {CMS} and {HELPDESK}; deterministic checks and bounded comparisons produce a cited review pack. The writer chooses priorities and reviews a drafted brief in the {DOCS}; approval through the {WORKFLOW} creates work items in the {PROJECT}. Technical changes require technical-owner acceptance before publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source versions and feedback were scattered, while rules covered only part of substantive review. Integration and maintenance often cost more than occasional manual reviews.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing style checks, version metadata and bounded text comparisons can support review. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, but the local benefit needs measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether instructions remain safe and complete requires technical expertise. Poor source control and unusual print or binding constraints still create expensive exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The writer weighs reader needs, technical consequences and production constraints, and notices omissions that comparison checks miss.

ambition.what: Monthly revision-priority review for the active manual catalogue.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time collecting editions and more time testing priorities with technical owners. With delegated authority, they can reorder low-risk editorial work; technical scope and publication approval remain with their owners.

reach.task: Plan a revision queue across related publications.
reach.learn: Editorial prioritisation, content dependencies and release planning.

reach.task: Compare reproduction and binding options.
reach.learn: Print specifications, production constraints and cost trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Repeatable terminology and house-style checks can support the mechanical part of review.
A vendor case reports fewer translation edits and shorter reviews; it does not establish this task's savings.
Version-linked comparisons and approval routing are feasible with controlled records and interfaces.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, informed by the supplied judgement-heavy priors.
Published manuals and approved specifications have identifiable versions.
Build ranges cover a small pilot; shared components overlap with other tasks.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Personal feedback is minimised and model access is controlled.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; approval waiting time may exceed build effort.
unknowns: How reliably published editions map to approved specifications.
Who may approve editorial, technical and production changes.
Whether reader feedback contains personal or confidential information.
Available interfaces and the applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: How many substantive discrepancies does a bounded comparison miss on previously reviewed manuals?
Does reviewing the generated pack take less time than the current review method?
new_work: Review cited discrepancies and reject false positives.
Route uncertain technical changes to technical owners.
Maintain source mappings, style rules and brief templates.
Monitor comparison quality and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Review published materials and recommend revisions or changes in scope, format, content, and methods of reproduction and binding.

tasks.short: Choose photographs, drawings, diagrams and charts that explain technical material.

steps.what: Read the draft and identify passages needing illustrations.
Search stored assets and request missing illustrations from technical colleagues.
Inspect candidate illustrations for technical accuracy, clarity and relevance.
Select illustrations and specify crops, annotations and placement.
Check usage rights, approved versions and production suitability.
Attach cleared assets and placement instructions to the publication draft.

tasks.design: Configure an asset catalogue in the {DOCS} with equipment identifiers, versions, rights and production metadata. Filters assemble candidates and deterministic checks flag missing permissions or unsuitable files; the writer selects the explanatory image and clears exceptions. The {WORKFLOW} packages cleared assets and placement instructions for the desktop publisher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Asset folders often lacked consistent identifiers, version records and reusable permissions. Choosing the clearest explanation remained a visual and technical judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata forms, file checks and document packaging already exist as standard capabilities. AI-assisted coding makes small validation and handoff extensions cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible illustration can show the wrong equipment variant or hide a hazard. Rights interpretation, technical validation and explanatory choices still need people.
tasks.human_edge: The writer chooses what the reader must see and recognises misleading perspective, missing context and unsafe crops.

ambition.what: Task-indexed illustration catalogue for technical publications.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time hunting files and more time checking whether images explain the task. They can curate reusable editorial selections; new technical depictions still require technical-owner validation.

reach.task: Brief a diagram that explains an operating sequence.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, perspective, annotation and diagram conventions.

reach.task: Specify accessible illustrations for digital manuals.
reach.learn: Text alternatives, contrast and responsive image behaviour.

evidence.claim: Metadata filters, file validation and asset packaging can reduce search and handoff work.
Selecting technically accurate explanatory images remains dependent on visual and domain judgement.

assumptions: The target uses existing approved images; it does not assume reliable generation of equipment illustrations.
Step shares reflect the supplied selection-heavy priors; search savings depend on metadata quality.
Build ranges exclude a large historical asset-cleanup project.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; identifiable people in photographs require appropriate handling.
Access effort includes employee consultation where national rules apply; no employee-performance monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Whether assets have searchable equipment identifiers and approved versions.
Completeness of rights records and any restrictions on crops or annotations.
Who validates new technical depictions.
Supported catalogue features and interfaces in the current {DOCS}.
research_questions: Can metadata filters retrieve useful candidates without semantic image matching?
Which file checks catch the most recurring production defects?
new_work: Tag new assets and repair incomplete catalogue records.
Resolve missing permissions and obsolete equipment variants.
Maintain production validation rules.
Review catalogue usefulness with writers and designers.
tasks.statement: Select photographs, drawings, sketches, diagrams, and charts to illustrate material.

tasks.short: Study technical sources and product samples to establish accurate operating procedures and production sequences.

steps.what: Collect current drawings, specifications, mockups and product references.
Read sources and map components, dependencies and operating conditions.

loop.input: Registered specifications and drawings for one product revision.
loop.output: Component and dependency map with page references and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate references and revision identifiers; writer verifies relationships and safety-relevant details.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per source section; unreadable or conflicting material becomes an open question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative specifications and drawing annotations describe relationships that fixed field extraction cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Inspect product samples and observe the actual operating sequence.
Discuss missing details and conflicting instructions with the technical engineer.
Document the operating procedure and production sequence from verified evidence.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence map, observation notes and engineer clarifications.
loop.output: Procedure and sequence brief with evidence references and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections and source coverage; writer verifies order, conditions and warnings.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; unsupported instructions remain blank and are escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning mixed technical evidence into clear procedural prose requires language synthesis.

steps.what: Approve technical accuracy and resolve remaining safety-critical uncertainties.

tasks.design: Configure revision-controlled source packs in the {DOCS}, with deterministic completeness checks and a bounded extraction loop producing an evidence map. A second bounded loop drafts the technical brief from reviewed evidence; physical observation, engineer clarification and technical approval remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used different formats and revisions. Understanding physical behaviour and undocumented dependencies required direct inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document metadata and inexpensive custom extraction tools can assemble referenced evidence and draft structured briefs. Faster AI-assisted coding lowers implementation effort without resolving technical uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Complex drawings, undocumented operating conditions and safety-critical sequencing still require product knowledge and physical validation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice where observed behaviour contradicts the specification and ask the engineer the question that prevents a dangerous instruction.

ambition.what: Pre-release documentation readiness review identifying missing operating evidence.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time assembling sources and more time observing products and resolving gaps. They gain a proposed documentation-readiness recommendation; engineering retains technical approval.

reach.task: Review whether a procedure gives readers the prerequisites and sequence they need.
reach.learn: Task analysis, evidence traceability and procedural editing.

evidence.claim: Source-linked technical extraction and brief generation are proposed designs, not demonstrated technical-writing cases in this digest.
Acrolinx provides repeatable style checks and quality gates; this supports language checks, not engineering validation.
A controlled professional-writing trial found productivity gains; its results do not establish savings for equipment analysis.

assumptions: This describes a company that documents physical equipment or technical products.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Source assembly is repetitive, but physical inspection and engineering judgement limit overall automation.
Use access-controlled processing under GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations. Assess consultation under national rules where employee-facing changes warrant it.
unknowns: Whether drawings and specifications have reliable revision identifiers.
Whether product samples and technical engineers are available.
Which procedures require formal safety or regulatory approval.
Whether access, processor terms or national consultation requirements delay implementation.
research_questions: Can extraction preserve drawing relationships and references on representative source packs?
Which evidence gaps are most predictive of later documentation corrections?
new_work: Review extracted relationships and evidence references.
Maintain revision mappings and source permissions.
Handle unreadable drawings and unresolved contradictions.
Evaluate draft quality against approved technical briefs.
tasks.statement: Study drawings, specifications, mockups, and product samples to integrate and delineate technology, operating procedure, and production sequence and detail.

tasks.short: Interview engineers and production staff, and read technical sources to understand products and production methods.

steps.what: Arrange interviews with engineers and production staff.
Read specifications, existing manuals and relevant technical literature.

loop.input: Approved source versions and the documentation brief.
loop.output: Source notes with quotations, page references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify cited passages exist; the writer checks technical meaning and source suitability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per source; unreadable or unsupported passages return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search finds passages, but specifications and literature express relevant details in varied prose.

steps.what: Prepare questions about unclear technology, terminology and production details.

loop.input: Source notes, unresolved questions and a standard interview checklist.
loop.output: Interview questions linked to source gaps.
loop.check: Require a source gap or checklist item for each question; the writer adjusts priorities.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous questions remain for the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: A checklist covers standard topics but cannot phrase questions about unfamiliar technical gaps.

steps.what: Interview specialists and probe assumptions, exceptions and practical production knowledge.
Combine interview findings and source notes into a technology brief.

loop.input: Interview notes and source notes with version references.
loop.output: Technology brief separating supported facts, disagreements and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Each factual statement needs a source reference; the writer checks conflicts and terminology.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unresolved conflicts remain explicitly marked.
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining differently worded explanations requires language interpretation beyond a fixed template.

steps.what: Confirm technical accuracy and resolve disputed explanations.

tasks.design: Configure interview scheduling through {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW}, and retrieve permitted source versions from {DOCS}. Small bounded loops extract cited notes, suggest interview questions and draft a technology brief; the writer conducts interviews and the engineering lead approves technical accuracy in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling was already automatable. Reading varied technical sources and combining tacit explanations needed custom language handling and reliable source links.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features, document retrieval and bounded text extraction can now be stitched together with less implementation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Tacit knowledge, conflicting specifications and safety implications still require specialists. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; access to internal material and any recording need an appropriate basis.
tasks.human_edge: The writer notices when a confident explanation hides an assumption and asks the question that exposes it.

ambition.what: Documentation readiness decisions at engineering change reviews

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time assembling notes and more time probing gaps before changes reach users. With delegated authority, they can flag documentation as unready at engineering change reviews; technical approval stays with engineering.

reach.task: Plan a technical publication around unresolved reader questions.
reach.learn: Learn editorial commissioning, audience definition and evidence-based publication planning.

reach.task: Interview users about confusing product terminology.
reach.learn: Learn neutral questioning, qualitative coding and the limits of small interview samples.

evidence.claim: Archive question answering is an existing capability, though the digest describes news archives rather than engineering documentation.
A professional writing trial found faster drafting; it does not establish technical accuracy or interview replacement.
Scheduling, version retrieval and source-linked brief generation are feasible building blocks; this task-specific design remains unvalidated.

assumptions: Interviews and document reading dominate today's work, consistent with the supplied priors.
The target uses an approved source collection rather than unrestricted browsing.
Build ranges cover one documentation team and a limited source collection.
Remaining percentages are design estimates, not measured customer savings.
unknowns: Where authoritative specifications and literature are stored and how versions are identified.
Whether source licences permit the proposed processing.
Who can approve technical explanations and documentation readiness.
Which employee consultation and access processes apply under national rules.
research_questions: How reliably does extraction preserve technical qualifiers, units and exceptions?
Which retrieval and citation checks best expose conflicting source versions?
new_work: Check cited passages and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain source access, version rules and interview checklists.
Sample briefs for omitted qualifications and unsupported conclusions.
Handle unavailable sources and failed extraction.
tasks.statement: Interview production and engineering personnel and read journals and other material to become familiar with product technologies and production methods.

tasks.short: Observe production and experiments to establish operating steps, conditions and practical details.

steps.what: Arrange access and observation time with production or development staff.
Read current procedures, equipment instructions and experiment plans.
Observe work, record sequence and conditions, and question unexpected actions.
Reconstruct operating steps, prerequisites, warnings and unresolved details.

loop.input: Observation notes, approved instructions and a procedure template.
loop.output: Procedure draft with evidence references and missing details marked.
loop.check: Require evidence for every operating instruction; the writer checks order, units and warnings.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; missing or contradictory instructions return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text observations need interpretation to become clear instructions; templates only provide structure.

steps.what: Validate the reconstructed procedure against actual operation and permitted conditions.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling in {CALENDAR} and an observation checklist in {WORKFLOW}, linked to current instructions in {DOCS}. The writer observes the work directly, then a bounded loop turns their notes into a referenced procedure draft in {DOCS}; the engineering lead validates it before approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: The central evidence exists in physical activity, including gestures, conditions and deviations that written records omit. Scheduling and templates could already help, but could not replace observation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms reduce preparation and missing fields. Bounded drafting can organize notes, with source links and explicit gaps.
tasks.still_hard: One observed run may not establish a safe or complete procedure. Rare conditions, experimental uncertainty and hazardous actions require engineering judgement and sometimes another observation.
tasks.human_edge: The writer distinguishes what happened once from what an operator should reliably do, and notices undocumented workarounds.
tasks.altitude: The writer gains modest preparation and paperwork savings, leaving more time to investigate unclear observations. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Review operating instructions for completeness and usable sequence.
reach.learn: Learn procedural editing, warning placement and how to distinguish evidence from inference.

reach.task: Plan visual explanations of difficult operating steps.
reach.learn: Learn visual sequencing, viewpoint selection and how to test whether an illustration resolves confusion.

evidence.claim: Structured checklists and document templates can reduce administration while direct observation remains human work.
The writing trial supports potential drafting assistance, but does not validate operating instructions or safety decisions.
Automated style checks can support procedure editing; they do not establish technical correctness.

assumptions: Direct observation is the largest time component, consistent with the supplied priors.
The target uses written notes and does not require continuous recording of workers.
A standard procedure template and an identifiable engineering approver exist.
Build ranges cover one procedure family; remaining percentages are estimates.
unknowns: Whether observed work involves hazardous equipment or regulated procedures.
Who authorizes site access and validates operating conditions.
Whether repeat observations are needed for variants and exceptional conditions.
What national employee consultation requirements apply to proposed observation records.
research_questions: Which checklist fields best reveal missing prerequisites and exceptional conditions?
How often does drafting introduce a step or warning absent from the supplied evidence?
new_work: Review drafted instructions against observation notes.
Track unresolved conditions and arrange targeted follow-up observations.
Maintain templates, required fields and source-version links.
Apply GDPR and EU AI Act requirements to the chosen processing and deployment.
tasks.statement: Observe production, developmental, and experimental activities to determine operating procedure and detail.

tasks.short: Arrange formatting, reproduction and controlled distribution of approved technical material.

steps.what: Send production requirements, source files and intended recipients to the publishing coordinator.
Prepare layouts and generate required digital and print versions.
Check the proof for missing content, broken references and layout errors.
Authorise the exact revision, audience, channels and print quantity.
Place the approved print order and confirm delivery requirements.
Release digital copies, notify recipients and record distribution.

tasks.design: Use structured production requests in the {WORKFLOW} and template-based generators fed by the {DOCS}. Bind release authorisation to the exact files, recipients and print order, then execute approved distribution through the {CMS}, {EMAIL} and {PROCUREMENT}; changed payloads require renewed approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layout preparation and distribution were coordinated through attachments and individual instructions. Publication metadata did not consistently travel with the files.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and publishing features handle much of the workflow. Small deterministic generators can fill remaining format and packaging gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Complex layouts, accessible output and physical printing exceptions need inspection. Incorrect audience selection remains consequential.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically correct publication is unsuitable for its audience, channel or release date.

ambition.what: Version-specific publication packs for service partners.

tasks.altitude: The writer reviews proofs and release exceptions instead of coordinating routine handoffs. Publication authority remains with the publication approver.

reach.task: Create reusable layouts for digital and printed technical material.
reach.learn: Template constraints, accessibility checks and print production requirements.

evidence.claim: Template rendering, approval routing and controlled distribution generally use deterministic software.
Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style checks and quality gates, a possible component of proof checking.

assumptions: Source material is normally digital; arranging typing now mainly means formatting and production.
Printed copies remain part of this representative workflow.
The review time for distribution gates is accounted for in the release-authorisation step.
Build ranges assume existing publishing and purchasing capabilities.
GDPR applies to recipient data; applicable EU AI Act duties apply if model-generated content enters the process. Consultation follows national rules where relevant.
unknowns: Which output formats, languages and accessibility requirements are mandatory.
Whether publication and purchasing systems expose usable approval mechanisms.

tasks.statement: Arrange for typing, duplication, and distribution of material.

tasks.short: Help arrange technical text and illustrations into publication-ready layouts.

steps.what: Collect approved text, illustrations, layout templates and production specifications.
Import content and apply styles in the {OTHER} publishing tool.
Adjust page breaks, tables and illustration placement in the {OTHER} publishing tool.
Review the rendered proof for readability, missing content and production defects.
Package the approved layout and assets using the {OTHER} publishing tool.

tasks.design: Configure reusable styles and import mappings in the {OTHER} publishing tool, with approved sources assembled from the {DOCS}. Deterministic preflight checks compare rendered content with source text and flag overflow, broken references and unsuitable assets. The writer handles layout exceptions and approves the proof before an internal production package is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent source formatting and exceptional tables or diagrams limited template reuse. Manual proof checking compensated for weak content structure and export validation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing publishing templates and export controls handle repeatable layout. AI-assisted coding can cheaply add content-completeness checks and connectors without requiring a model to design pages.
tasks.still_hard: Dense diagrams, multilingual expansion and unusual tables need visual judgement. Rendering can change across fonts and environments, so technical instructions must be checked in the actual output.
tasks.human_edge: The writer keeps warnings, steps and illustrations together so readers can understand and follow the instruction.

ambition.what: Accessible digital manual edition from the same approved content.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time applying styles and more time resolving difficult reading sequences and layout exceptions. They gain capacity to specify reusable templates; final production release retains its existing approver.

tasks.short: Assess field developments and decide which published materials need revision or replacement.

steps.what: Collect release notes, standards notices, and relevant field publications.
Compare developments with published instructions and identify potentially affected sections.

loop.input: New source passages and published sections selected by identifiers, versions, and terminology.
loop.output: Candidate affected sections with paired source passages and proposed impact categories.
loop.check: Require valid source and section references; writer reviews relevance and samples unmatched developments.
loop.stop: One assessment and one repair pass per source item; uncertain matches enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact identifiers handle explicit links, but changes expressed in different language need semantic comparison.

steps.what: Discuss applicability, technical consequences, and urgency with the writer.
Decide whether to revise, create new material, or take no action.
Write the revision brief with affected sections, sources, and acceptance criteria.
Create revision work items and link the supporting brief in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects approved change sources and matches explicit identifiers against the document register in the {DOCS}. A bounded comparison loop proposes an impact map; human decisions feed template-generated revision briefs and linked work items in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Developments and published sections lacked reliable links. Keyword searches missed changes expressed through different terminology.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic collection and version matching narrow the material needing semantic comparison. Bounded models can propose evidence-linked matches for review.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete coverage can hide an important development. Applicability, urgency, safety implications, and competing priorities remain judgments.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a development changes real operating practice and when apparent novelty needs no documentation change.
tasks.altitude: The writer can run a short weekly impact review instead of periodically rebuilding the evidence. Revision, safety, and release decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess which field developments affect customer information needs.
reach.learn: Source reliability, trend validation, and customer-segment relevance.

Archive question-answering is being tested in publishing; the digest provides no technical-manual impact-analysis case.
Identifier matching, bounded semantic comparison, and decision-driven brief generation form a plausible design requiring local validation.

Revision decisions capture reasons and acceptance criteria in structured fields.
Collection automates known sources; it does not guarantee discovery of every relevant development.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant. Source access rights and national consultation rules must be respected.

tasks.short: Review equipment source material to establish reliable operation, maintenance and service facts.

steps.what: Gather manufacturer catalogs, drawings and service documents for the equipment.
Check equipment identifiers, revision dates and source applicability.
Read operation, maintenance and service requirements and record supporting references.

loop.input: Applicable catalogs, drawings and service documents for identified equipment revisions.
loop.output: Referenced facts covering operating limits, maintenance intervals, service conditions and warnings.
loop.check: Validate units, identifiers and page references; writer checks conditions, exceptions and safety-relevant entries.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document section; unreadable details remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in prose, tables and annotations, with qualifications that fixed extraction rules can miss.

steps.what: Compare sources and identify missing, inconsistent or superseded requirements.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence entries and source-applicability exceptions.
loop.output: Potential contradictions and missing conditions with both supporting references.
loop.check: Compare numeric fields deterministically; writer verifies semantic conflicts and rejects false matches.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass per equipment item; unresolved conflicts go to engineering.
loop.why_not_simpler: Different wording can conceal incompatible instructions even when identifiers and numeric values match.

steps.what: Resolve technical conflicts or record that further evidence is required.
Store reviewed facts, unresolved questions and source references for later writing.

tasks.design: Configure source intake from the {PARTNER_PORTAL} into the {DOCS}, then use deterministic equipment and revision matching to flag exceptions. Bounded extraction and reconciliation loops build referenced evidence and conflict registers. Engineering resolves technical conflicts, and the {DOCS} preserves approved facts alongside unresolved questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier material was file-based, inconsistently indexed and difficult to compare. Similar equipment names concealed different revisions and service requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can populate a stable evidence schema, while simple identifier and unit checks catch routine mismatches. AI-assisted coding makes these small integrations cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Obsolete supplier files, conditional warnings and undocumented equipment modifications can invalidate apparently clear facts. Engineering may need supplier clarification or inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a catalog statement does not apply to the installed equipment and refuse to turn uncertainty into an instruction.

ambition.what: Equipment documentation gap register for maintenance planning.

tasks.altitude: The writer reviews evidence exceptions rather than repeatedly searching catalogs. They can recommend which documentation gaps need investigation; maintenance and engineering retain operating decisions.

reach.task: Check that technical claims carry the conditions and evidence needed for publication.
reach.learn: Source provenance, revision applicability and editing conditional instructions.

evidence.claim: Revision matching, unit validation and evidence registers can use deterministic software; mixed-document interpretation needs validation.
The digest provides no documented equipment-source extraction case establishing these proposed savings or build ranges.

Routine collection is automatable where authorised file access exists; inaccessible portals remain exceptions.

tasks.short: Create technical sketches showing materials, components and assembly order.

steps.what: Retrieve current drawings, component identifiers and assembly instructions from the engineering drawing application.
Agree the view, material details and assembly sequence with engineering.
Draw component views and assembly stages in the technical illustration application.
Add labels, callouts and sequence arrows in the technical illustration application.
Check component identity, orientation, material details and assembly order.

tasks.design: A deterministic exporter reads versioned engineering drawings and component identifiers from the engineering drawing application in {OTHER}, linked to approved instructions in {DOCS}. It generates editable views, callouts and sequence arrows for the technical illustration application in {OTHER}; the writer adjusts visual clarity and the engineering lead approves the sketch in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawing formats, component identifiers and illustration templates were poorly connected. Geometry reuse was possible, but building and maintaining exporters often cost more than occasional manual sketches.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing drawing export interfaces and reusable vector templates provide the foundation. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting formats and placing callouts without generating new geometry.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy drawings, missing assembly structure and crowded views need manual work. Showing orientation, hidden parts and material differences clearly requires technical and visual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The writer chooses the view that reveals the reader's likely mistake and removes detail that obscures the assembly action.
tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time tracing components and numbering labels, and more time testing whether readers understand the sequence. With a broader remit, they can choose which common assembly mistakes deserve dedicated visual guidance; engineering retains technical approval.

reach.learn: Learn information hierarchy, accessible symbol design and visual comprehension testing.

evidence.claim: Structured engineering geometry can support deterministic view export and identifier-based callouts.
The digest supplies no documented case for assembly illustration generation; savings depend on reusable source geometry.
Reader viewpoint, visual ambiguity and technical approval remain human responsibilities in this design.

tasks.short: Create and update online help that explains verified product behaviour and user procedures.

steps.what: Collect release changes, support issues and existing help articles.
Identify affected topics and decide which changes need new instructions.

loop.input: Release changes, de-identified support issues and indexed help topics.
loop.output: Proposed affected topics, coverage gaps and reasons linked to sources.
loop.check: Validate topic identifiers and citations; writer checks scope and priority.
loop.stop: One classification and one correction pass per release; unclear changes become open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text change descriptions and reader problems rarely share exact vocabulary with existing help topics.

steps.what: Draft or revise help topics, prerequisites and troubleshooting instructions.

loop.input: Approved topic plan, current articles and verified product evidence.
loop.output: Tracked article changes with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate schema, references and supported claims; writer reviews clarity and procedural completeness.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per topic; missing evidence blocks the affected instruction.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure but cannot compose clear instructions from varied source prose.

steps.what: Test instructions in a product test environment and resolve incorrect behaviour.
Check terminology, style, links, navigation and article formatting.
Approve article accuracy, reader suitability and release readiness.
Publish the approved revision and update the help index.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration assembles changes from the {PROJECT}, de-identified issues from the {HELPDESK} and current articles from the {CMS}. Bounded loops propose affected topics and source-linked drafts, while configured terminology and link checks handle routine quality control. The writer tests instructions, and the {CMS} publishes only the revision authorised by the documentation lead.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes and reader problems were scattered across teams. Drafting depended on interpreting incomplete descriptions and manually finding affected articles.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured article stores, change feeds and inexpensive integrations support repeatable intake. Bounded drafting can reduce prose work when verified sources are available.
tasks.still_hard: Documentation cannot establish product truth from incomplete release notes. Version differences, permissions and complex troubleshooting need hands-on validation.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipate the user's mistaken assumption and test whether the instructions actually help them finish the task.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of help gaps using recurring support problems.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more of the week testing procedures and choosing which reader problems deserve attention. They gain delegated topic-priority decisions within the agreed release scope.
